assessments.reasoning: Authenticity. The exact release tag resolves to the pinned publisher commit. The bytes came from that repository's Doc/reference/simple_stmts.rst at that commit. Integrity. The SHA-256 of the full independently downloaded response matches the registered source revision. Relevance. Simple statements lines 1008–1023 explicitly identify the nearest enclosing binding and the SyntaxError case. Execution model lines 105–109 and 146–156 explain visibility, global declarations, and the type-parameter exception. Interpretation. Nearest applies to the binding that is visible and eligible under lexical scope rules. The wording about previous bindings is static and allows the enclosing binding operation to execute after the declaration. A same-named class attribute or module binding does not supply an eligible enclosing function-local binding. Applicability. The release and descriptive modality match, but the frozen condition only requires a nonlocal declaration and an enclosing function scope. A physically enclosing function can bind the name while that binding is unavailable to the inner declaration because another enclosing function declares it global. The frozen condition needs to express eligibility or visibility. Type parameters belong to annotation scopes and cannot be rebound via nonlocal. Contradiction. The cited descriptive passage does document the nearest binding and absent-binding error. The adverse case challenges application of that shorthand to all textually enclosing bindings. The reference's adjacent scope and global rules and the exact release's implementation support distinguishing an unavailable binding from a usable one.

challenge.method: Read both exact documentation chapters and the publisher's PEP 3104. Compiled locally authored nested-scope cases with no intermediate binding, two function bindings, a same-named intervening class attribute, a module global only, an outer assignment after the declaration, an intervening function global declaration, and a type parameter. For the global-declaration case, inspected the pinned v3.13.0 compiler's bound-set analysis.
challenge.results: Test cases on CPython 3.13.5 selected the outer binding if the intervening function had none, selected the closer binding when both bound the name, and skipped a class attribute. A later outer assignment provided a lexical binding. A module global alone and a type parameter produced SyntaxError. An intermediate global declaration also produced SyntaxError with a farther lexical binding present. Exact v3.13.0 symtable code removes an explicitly global name from the available bound set and rejects nonlocal if that set has no such name. The simple nearest-textual-binding interpretation exceeds the documented visibility rules.

limitations: The claim is descriptive. The compiler is a challenge source for applicability and supplies no independent language specification.
Runtime challenge cases ran on CPython 3.13.5. The intervening-global mechanism was also checked directly in v3.13.0 source.
Qualify the condition by requiring an eligible, lexically visible binding in an enclosing function. A bare reference to textual enclosure cannot cover the adverse case.
